pure-announcement.rationale: OPA's own architecture and getting-started documentation for a project that has existed since 2016 and graduated CNCF in 2021, not a launch or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: Nearest concepts address a different axis — which pipeline stage catches which failure class (layered-agent-guardrails), or tool-call ergonomics — not the internal expressiveness of the decision mechanism itself; layered-agent-guardrails even names a static allow/deny list as one of its layers, which this concept would let someone upgrade.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Primary project documentation with a live public playground, open-source implementation, and runnable examples — directly checkable, not merely asserted.

durability.rationale: The decouple-decision-from-enforcement architecture and arbitrary-structured-output model have been stable since 2016 and are the de facto standard for policy-as-code (Kubernetes admission control, API gateways, CI/CD) — a durable mechanism, not a pricing or version detail.

actionability.rationale: Gives a concrete adoptable pattern — query a decoupled engine with structured input plus external data, receive structured (not just allow/deny) decisions — that directly enables encoding budgets, rate limits, or computed risk scores as policy conditions, changing how someone would design an authorization layer.

atomicity.rationale: The note bundles the architectural claim with a full hands-on Rego syntax tutorial (variables, rules, functions, imports, a worked network-policy example) and CLI installation instructions — several separable ideas beyond the one durable architectural principle.
